family_title: Hugging Face PEFT library inventory (tuners, LoRA variants, optimizers and merge utilities)

methods.name: LoRA
methods.paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0 x + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A x,\quad W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (PEFT also: Embedding, Conv1d/2d/3d, MultiheadAttention, raw nn.Parameter e.g. MoE experts via target_parameters); originally W_q, W_v, commonly 'all-linear'
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space: \Delta W = BA, \operatorname{rank}\Delta W \le r
methods.mergeable_reason: BA is a dense d_out x d_in matrix that can be added to W_0 after training (merge_and_unload), giving zero inference overhead.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (A Kaiming-uniform in PEFT, Gaussian in the paper; init_lora_weights='gaussian' keeps B = 0); scaling alpha/r.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning updates have low intrinsic rank, so freeze W_0 and learn only a rank-r factorization of the update.
methods.results_note: Paper reports on-par or better quality than full fine-tuning on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2 and GPT-3 175B, with 10,000x fewer trainable parameters and 3x less GPU memory for GPT-3.

relations.note: Mergeable alternative to serial bottleneck adapters, so no extra inference latency.
Fixed-rank special case of AdaLoRA's adaptive SVD-shaped budget.

methods.name: AdaLoRA
methods.paper_title: AdaLoRA: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + P\Lambda Q,\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r),\ Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \mathcal{L}_{tot}=\mathcal{L}+\gamma\big(\|P^\top P-I\|_F^2+\|QQ^\top-I\|_F^2\big);\ \lambda_i \text{ masked by sensitivity-based importance to meet a global rank budget}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}+1) \text{ with } r=\text{init\_r}, \text{ pruned to an average of target\_r}
methods.locus: any linear layer (PEFT: also Conv2d since v0.20)
methods.structure: SVD-shaped low-rank update P\Lambda Q with near-orthogonal P,Q and a learned per-matrix rank (masked singular values)
methods.mergeable_reason: P Lambda Q is a dense low-rank matrix that can be added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Lambda = 0 (P, Q Gaussian), so Delta W = 0; a warmup (tinit), budget-reduction and final phase are scheduled via update_and_allocate.
methods.key_idea: Different weight matrices deserve different ranks; parameterize the update in SVD form and prune unimportant singular values to reallocate a global parameter budget.
methods.results_note: Reports notable gains over LoRA and other baselines, especially in low-budget settings, on GLUE, SQuAD and summarization with DeBERTaV3/BART.

relations.note: Fixed-rank LoRA is AdaLoRA without budget reallocation.
Both reallocate ranks across layers (EVA from activation variance, AdaLoRA from importance scores).

methods.name: AdaMSS
methods.full_name: Adaptive Multi-Subspace Approach for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.paper_title: AdaMSS: Adaptive Multi-Subspace Approach for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W_0\approx U_R\Sigma_RV_R^\top;\ \text{rows of } U_R \text{ clustered into } K \text{ subspaces } S_1,\dots,S_K;\ (\Delta W)_{S_k,:}=B_kA_kV_R^\top,\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{|S_k|\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times R};\ V_R \text{ frozen},\ A_k,B_k \text{ trained; ASA prunes low-importance subspaces}
methods.structure: output rows partitioned into K clusters (subspace segmentation of the top-R left singular vectors); each cluster gets its own low-rank update inside the frozen top-R right singular subspace of W_0
methods.mergeable_reason: The scattered block-low-rank update is a fixed matrix after training and can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B_k = 0 (A_k initialized from a QR of the subspace data); requires an SVD + KMeans clustering of W_0 at injection time.
methods.key_idea: Replace one big low-rank subspace with several smaller, data-segmented subspaces and adaptively keep only the subspaces most relevant to the task.
methods.results_note: Abstract reports +4.7% average accuracy over LoRA on ViT-Large with 15.4% of LoRA's trainable parameters, and +7% over PiSSA on RoBERTa-Large with about 94.4% fewer parameters.

relations.note: Both start from the SVD of W_0; AdaMSS splits it into multiple subspaces.
Adaptive Subspace Allocation prunes subspaces via importance scores, analogous to AdaLoRA's budget allocation.

methods.name: LLaMA-Adapter
methods.paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
methods.formula_latex: \text{top } L' \text{ layers: } \mathrm{Attn}(q)=\big[\,g_l\cdot\mathrm{softmax}(qK_P^\top/\sqrt{d});\ \mathrm{softmax}(qK^\top/\sqrt{d})\,\big]\,[V_P;V],\ K_P=P_lW_k,\ V_P=P_lW_v,\ P_l\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times d} \text{ (adaption prompt)},\ g_l=0 \text{ at init}
methods.trainable_params: L'(K d + 1) \ \ (K=\text{adapter\_len},\ L'=\text{adapter\_layers}; \text{one scalar gate per layer in PEFT})
methods.locus: keys/values of the top L' self-attention layers (learned adaption-prompt tokens)
methods.structure: learned prompt vectors attended to at the top layers, whose softmax-normalized attention contribution is multiplied by a zero-initialized gate
methods.mergeable_reason: The extra attended tokens and gated attention branch are not a weight-space change and cannot be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Gate g_l = 0, so the adaption prompts contribute nothing at initialization (zero-init attention).
methods.key_idea: Inject instruction knowledge through a few prompt tokens at the top layers, using zero-gated attention so training starts exactly from the pretrained model.
methods.results_note: Paper reports turning LLaMA-7B into an instruction follower with 1.2M learnable parameters in under one hour on 8 A100s, comparable to fully fine-tuned Alpaca.

relations.note: Layer-wise learned key/value tokens, restricted to top layers and gated.
Both learn soft tokens; LLaMA-Adapter injects them inside attention with a zero gate.

methods.name: BEFT
methods.paper_title: BEFT: Bias-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models in Low-Data Regimes
methods.formula_latex: h = W_v x + b_v + \Delta b_v,\ \ \Delta b_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ trained, all weights frozen};\ \ a(V+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top)=aV+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top \text{ (rows of } a \text{ sum to 1)}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} \text{ per value projection } (\approx 0.01\% \text{ of parameters})
methods.locus: bias of the value projection W_v in every attention block (bias added, zero-initialized, for bias-free LLMs)
methods.structure: additive shift of the value-projection output; because attention rows sum to one, the shift passes straight to the attention output
methods.mergeable_reason: It is just a new bias value; it folds into the existing bias, but bias-free models (e.g. LLaMA) gain a bias vector they did not have.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained bias (or a zero-initialized added bias), so the function is unchanged.
methods.key_idea: Among q/k/v biases, fine-tuning only the value bias b_v gives the best accuracy per parameter in low-data regimes.
methods.results_note: Paper reports b_v fine-tuning consistently beating b_q and b_k fine-tuning across encoder- and decoder-only LLMs up to 6.7B, with about 9x fewer parameters than tuning all biases.

relations.note: Restricts BitFit to a single bias term (value projection).
Both are vector-sized interventions on attention; IA3 scales, BEFT shifts.

methods.name: BOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning via Butterfly Factorization
methods.formula_latex: W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,W_0R^\top,\ \ R=\prod_{i=1}^{m}P_i^\top\,\mathrm{blockdiag}(R_{i,1},\dots,R_{i,d_{in}/b})\,P_i\in SO(d_{in}),\ R_{i,j}=(I+Q_{i,j})(I-Q_{i,j})^{-1},\ Q_{i,j}^\top=-Q_{i,j}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b}
methods.locus: any linear / Conv2d layer (rotation of the input space of W_0)
methods.structure: orthogonal R \in SO(d_{in}) built as a product of m butterfly-permuted block-diagonal orthogonal factors (Cooley-Tukey style), plus an output magnitude vector s
methods.mergeable_reason: diag(s) W_0 R^T is a single dense matrix that replaces W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 so every block is the identity (R = I) and s = 1.
methods.key_idea: Make orthogonal fine-tuning cheap by factorizing the dense orthogonal matrix into sparse butterfly factors, as in the FFT.
methods.results_note: Paper reports favorable results versus OFT and LoRA when fine-tuning large ViTs, LLMs and text-to-image diffusion models, with fewer parameters than block-diagonal OFT.

relations.note: With m = 1 butterfly factor BOFT reduces to block-diagonal OFT.
Alternative structured parameterization of an orthogonal multiplicative update.

methods.name: C³A
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+\mathcal{C}_{blk}(\Delta w)\,x,\ \ (\Delta h)_i=\sum_{j=1}^{d_{in}/b}\Delta w_{ij}\star x_j,\ \Delta w_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{b},\ \ \Delta w\star x \text{ computed with FFTs}
methods.structure: block-circulant \Delta W: a (d_{out}/b)\times(d_{in}/b) grid of b\times b circulant blocks; rank is decoupled from the parameter count
methods.mergeable_reason: The block-circulant matrix can be materialized and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: NOT an identity by default in PEFT (kernels Xavier-uniform initialized); init_weights=True zero-initializes the kernels for an exact no-op.
methods.key_idea: Use circular convolution kernels (circulant matrices) so the update can be high-rank while costing only d_in*d_out/b parameters and FFT-time compute.
methods.results_note: Paper reports GLUE avg 86.96 vs 85.96 for LoRA (RoBERTa-Large) and 85.9 vs 83.9 on 8 commonsense tasks for LLaMA3-8B with 37% fewer parameters.

relations.note: Both exploit the Fourier domain; FourierFT learns sparse spectra, C3A learns circulant kernels.
High-rank alternative at LoRA-level parameter and memory cost.

methods.name: Cartridges
methods.paper_title: Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long context representations via self-study
methods.formula_latex: \forall l:\ K_l\leftarrow[Z_k^{(l)};K_l],\ V_l\leftarrow[Z_v^{(l)};V_l],\ Z_k^{(l)},Z_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times d};\ \ \min_Z\sum_{(x,\tilde c)}\sum_i D_{KL}\big(F(\cdot\mid\tilde c\oplus x_{:i})\,\|\,F_Z(\cdot\mid x_{:i})\big)
methods.locus: keys/values at every layer (a directly parameterized KV-cache prefix)
methods.structure: learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, trained directly (no MLP reparameterization) by context distillation on synthetic self-study conversations about a corpus
methods.mergeable_reason: The cartridge is extra KV state attended by the model, not a weight change.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity: initialized from the real prefill KV cache of the first p corpus tokens (or randomly); the first token is frozen as an attention sink.
methods.key_idea: Compress a long corpus offline into a small trainable KV cache via self-study distillation, so it can replace in-context documents at inference.
methods.results_note: Paper reports matching ICL quality with 38.6x less memory and 26.4x higher throughput, and extending effective context to 484k tokens.

relations.note: Same serving mechanism (past_key_values), but the KV prefix itself is the parameter and is distilled from a corpus.

methods.name: CPT
methods.paper_title: Context-aware Prompt Tuning: Advancing In-Context Learning with Adversarial Methods
methods.formula_latex: X_{ctx}=[T_i(x_i),S_{intra},T_o(y_i),S_{inter}]_{i=1}^{N};\ E\leftarrow\Pi_{\|E-E_0\|_2\le\epsilon}\big(E-\eta\nabla_E\mathcal{L}\big);\ \mathcal{L}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\gamma^{N+1-k}\,\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(k)},t_O^{(k)})+\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(N+1)},t_O^{(N+1)})
methods.trainable_params: \ell\,d \ \ (\ell=\text{number of context input/format tokens optimized; label tokens frozen})
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (embeddings of the in-context demonstrations)
methods.structure: soft prompt initialized from real few-shot demonstrations; per-token embedding changes projected onto an L2 ball (projected gradient descent) with a recency-decayed context loss
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimized context tokens are extra inputs, not weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not a no-op relative to the bare query: at init it equals ordinary in-context learning with the given demonstrations.
methods.key_idea: Treat the in-context demonstrations themselves as trainable soft prompts, but keep them within an epsilon-ball of the real tokens and down-weight early examples to counter recency bias.
methods.results_note: Paper reports gains over LoRA, prompt tuning, IPT and ICL on SST-2, AG News, DBpedia and TREC in 2/4/6-shot settings with BLOOM-1.7B, GPT-J-6B and Llama-3-8B.

relations.note: Soft prompt over demonstration tokens with projected (adversarial-style) updates.

methods.name: DEFT
methods.paper_title: DEFT: Decompositional Efficient Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Image Models
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0+QR,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(P),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{(PEFT default 'relu'): } W=(I-P\,\mathrm{relu}(P)^\top)W_0+PR
methods.locus: Linear / Conv1D layers (mainly text-to-image diffusion transformers/UNets)
methods.structure: rank-r update that removes an r-dimensional output subspace of W_0 and injects new content into it: \Delta W = Q(R - Q^\top W_0)
methods.mergeable_reason: The update equals a low-rank additive delta Q(R - Q^T W_0) that can be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT initializes R so that the injection exactly cancels the removal (W = W_0 at init); the paper initializes P at zero.
methods.key_idea: Split adaptation into 'forget a subspace' (projection) and 'write new content there' (low-rank injection) to personalize while preserving the base model's instruction-following/editability.
methods.results_note: Paper reports DreamBench Plus CLIP-T 0.361 on SDXL vs 0.341 for LoRA and 0.354 for PaRa.

relations.note: Dropping the injection term QR gives PaRa (DeftConfig(para=True)).
Same rank-r parameter budget, different (subspace-replacing) structure.

methods.name: PaRa
methods.paper_title: PaRa: Personalizing Text-to-Image Diffusion via Parameter Rank Reduction
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(B),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ trained}
methods.locus: attention/linear layers of text-to-image diffusion models
methods.structure: left-multiplication of W_0 by an orthogonal projector of corank r, shrinking the output space of the layer (rank reduction)
methods.mergeable_reason: (I - QQ^T) W_0 is a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity: PEFT notes PaRa cannot be a no-op at initialization since only the projection is trained.
methods.key_idea: Personalization works by reducing the rank of generation: projecting out a few output directions narrows the model's output space toward the target concept.
methods.results_note: Paper reports about 2x fewer parameters than LoRA and 82-97% human preference over LoRA across tested concepts.

relations.note: DEFT without the injection term.
Subtractive (rank-reducing) instead of additive low-rank adaptation.

methods.name: DeLoRA
methods.paper_title: DeLoRA: Decoupling Angles and Strength in Low-rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\frac{\lambda\|W_0\|}{r}\,B\,\Xi\,A,\ \ \Xi=\mathrm{diag}\Big(\tfrac{1}{\|b_i\|\,\|a_i\|}\Big),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \lambda \text{ trainable}
methods.structure: sum of r unit-Frobenius rank-1 terms with a learnable global strength, so \|\Delta W\|_F\le\lambda\|W_0\| (a Frobenius-ball boundary)
methods.mergeable_reason: The normalized low-rank update is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Paper: subtract a frozen copy of the initial update from W_0; PEFT default: B = 0 (A Kaiming) with lambda initialized to delora_lambda.
methods.key_idea: Normalize the low-rank directions and learn their strength separately, bounding how far the weights can drift and making training robust to learning rate and length.
methods.results_note: Paper reports GLUE avg 85.6 vs 84.7 for LoRA, parity with LoRA/DoRA on subject-driven generation, and better robustness to learning rate and extended training.

relations.note: Also decouples direction and magnitude, but normalizes the update rather than the full weight.
Extends bounded ETHER-style transformations to arbitrary rank with learnable strength.

methods.name: FourierFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Discrete Fourier Transform
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\alpha\,\mathrm{Re}\big(\mathcal{F}^{-1}_{2D}(F)\big),\ F\in\mathbb{C}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ zero except at } n \text{ fixed random frequency locations (shared across layers) holding trainable } c\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
methods.structure: \Delta W is the real part of the inverse 2D DFT of a sparse spectral matrix with n learnable coefficients
methods.mergeable_reason: The spatial-domain Delta W can be computed once and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT default init_weights=False draws coefficients from N(0,1), so it is NOT an exact identity; init_weights=True zero-initializes for a no-op.
methods.key_idea: Weight updates are compressible in the frequency domain, so learn only a handful of spectral coefficients.
methods.results_note: Paper reports outperforming LoRA on LLaMA2-7B instruction tuning with 0.064M trainable parameters versus LoRA's 33.5M.

relations.note: Both are Fourier-domain parameterizations of Delta W.
Same sparse-transform-coefficient idea with a wavelet instead of Fourier basis.

methods.name: FRoD
methods.full_name: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees
methods.paper_title: FRoD: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees for Fast Convergence
methods.formula_latex: W_i'=U_i(\Sigma_i+S_i)V^\top,\ \ U_i=Q_iZ,\ V^\top \text{ shared across layers of a module type (hierarchical joint decomposition)};\ \Sigma_i \text{ diagonal and } S_i \text{ sparse (density } s) \text{ trained; } U_i,V \text{ frozen}
methods.structure: full-rank core update in a frozen, cross-layer-shared basis: \Delta W_i = U_i(\Delta\Sigma_i+S_i)V^\top with diagonal ('on-axis' strength) plus sparse off-diagonal ('rotational') coefficients
methods.mergeable_reason: U_i(Sigma_i + S_i)V^T reconstructs a dense weight that replaces W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: S_i = 0 and Sigma_i taken from the decomposition, so the reconstruction reproduces W_0 at init (up to decomposition error); costly joint-decomposition setup.
methods.key_idea: Express updates as small rotations around a shared spectral basis, giving full-rank capacity with sparse trainable coefficients and fast convergence.
methods.results_note: Paper reports peak accuracy within 1-4 epochs and GLUE 90.53 vs 90.42 for full fine-tuning using about 2.5% of parameters.

relations.note: Both operate in a spectral basis of W_0; FRoD trains a sparse full-rank core instead of a rank-r factor.
Shared frozen bases with small per-layer trainable coefficients.

methods.name: GLoRA
methods.paper_title: One-for-All: Generalized LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: h=(W_0+W_0\odot A+B)\,x+b_0+b_0\odot D+E+W_0C;\ \ A,B\in\{\text{LoRA},\text{vector},\text{scalar},\text{none}\},\ C\in\{\text{LoRA},\text{vector},\text{none}\},\ D,E\in\{\text{vector},\text{scalar},\text{none}\}
methods.structure: unified reparameterization: Hadamard rescaling of W_0, additive (low-rank) weight shift, bias rescaling/shift, and a W_0-coupled bias (layer-wise prompt) path; per-layer path types chosen by evolutionary search in the paper
methods.mergeable_reason: All paths are linear in the parameters and fold into W_uni = W_0 + W_0*A + B and b_uni = b_0 + b_0*D + E + W_0 C.
methods.identity_at_init: Zero-initialized down-projections make every path zero (no-op) by default.
methods.key_idea: Subsume LoRA, scaling/shifting and prompt-like methods in one reparameterizable layer and search the best path configuration per layer.
methods.results_note: Paper reports 78.0% average on VTAB-1K, up to 2.9% above prior methods, and strong few-shot and domain-generalization results.

relations.note: B path in LoRA mode with all other paths disabled is LoRA.
The W_0 (.) A path with a LoRA-type A is HiRA's update (PEFT's elementwise implementation).
Vector-mode A path is a per-channel rescaling of W_0.

methods.name: GraLoRA
methods.paper_title: GraLoRA: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\begin{bmatrix}B_{11}A_{11}&\cdots&B_{1k}A_{1k}\\\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\B_{k1}A_{k1}&\cdots&B_{kk}A_{kk}\end{bmatrix},\ B_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{k}\times\frac{r}{k}},\ A_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{k}\times\frac{d_{in}}{k}}
methods.structure: k\times k block matrix of independent rank-(r/k) LoRAs, effective rank up to kr at LoRA's parameter count (optional hybrid with a vanilla LoRA part)
methods.mergeable_reason: The block matrix is a fixed dense update.
methods.identity_at_init: Every B_ij = 0.
methods.key_idea: Partition the weight into a grid and give each block its own small adapter, removing LoRA's gradient entanglement across channels and raising effective rank.
methods.results_note: Paper reports up to +8.5% absolute Pass@1 on HumanEval+ at rank 128 over LoRA, plus gains on commonsense and math reasoning.

relations.note: k = 1 recovers LoRA.
Both impose block structure on LoRA (GraLoRA for expressivity, BD-LoRA for TP serving).

methods.name: HiRA
methods.paper_title: HiRA: Parameter-Efficient Hadamard High-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+W_0\odot(BA),\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}
methods.structure: element-wise (Hadamard) modulation of W_0 by 1 + BA; \operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le r\cdot\operatorname{rank}W_0, i.e. high-rank at LoRA cost
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 + W_0 (.) BA is a dense matrix computable after training.
methods.key_idea: Multiply the frozen weight elementwise by a low-rank matrix so the update inherits W_0's full rank while the parameter count stays LoRA-sized.
methods.results_note: Paper (ICLR 2025 oral) reports outperforming LoRA and its variants on commonsense reasoning, dialogue generation and mathematical reasoning.

relations.note: GLoRA's weight-scaling path W_0 (.) A with a LoRA-type A.
Both use Hadamard products to escape the rank bound; LoHa multiplies two learned low-rank factors.

methods.name: HRA
methods.paper_title: Bridging The Gap between Low-rank and Orthogonal Adaptation via Householder Reflection Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0H,\ \ H=\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Big(I-2\frac{u_iu_i^\top}{\|u_i\|^2}\Big),\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}};\ \ \text{optional } \lambda\|I-U^\top U\|_F^2 \text{ (or Gram-Schmidt, apply\_GS)}
methods.locus: linear and Conv2d layers (rotation of the input space)
methods.structure: product of r Householder reflections (orthogonal) acting on the input side of W_0; equivalently W_0 + W_0U\Gamma U^\top, an 'adaptive LoRA'
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 H is a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Reflection vectors initialized in identical pairs (u_{2i} = u_{2i-1}), so consecutive reflections cancel and H = I; requires even r in PEFT.
methods.key_idea: A chain of r Householder reflections is simultaneously an orthogonal transform and a rank-r additive update, bridging OFT and LoRA.
methods.results_note: Paper reports better accuracy than LoRA/OFT-style baselines with fewer parameters on GLUE, LLaMA2-7B math reasoning, and subject-driven/controllable image generation.

relations.note: Orthogonal multiplicative update with a different (reflection-based) parameterization.
W_0 H = W_0 + W_0 U Gamma U^T is a rank-r additive update whose factors depend on W_0.

methods.name: (IA)³
methods.full_name: Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations
methods.paper_title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
methods.formula_latex: k=l_k\odot(W_kx),\ v=l_v\odot(W_vx),\ h_{ff}=W_2\big(l_{ff}\odot\gamma(W_1x)\big);\ l_k,l_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ l_{ff}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{ff}} \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} \text{ per key/value projection},\ d_{ff} \text{ per FFN}
methods.locus: outputs of key/value projections and inputs of the FFN down-projection (feedforward_modules)
methods.structure: diagonal scaling: W=\mathrm{diag}(l)W_0 (output rows) or W=W_0\mathrm{diag}(l) (FFN input columns)
methods.mergeable_reason: Diagonal scalings fold into the rows/columns of W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Scaling vectors l initialized to 1.
methods.key_idea: Learn only rescaling vectors that inhibit or amplify inner activations; with the T-Few recipe this beats in-context learning cheaply.
methods.results_note: Paper reports T-Few (T0 + (IA)^3) outperforming GPT-3 in-context learning and reaching super-human performance on RAFT.

relations.note: Vector-sized (rank-free) alternative with far fewer parameters.
GLoRA's vector-mode weight-scaling path.

methods.name: Lily
methods.paper_title: Low-Rank Interconnected Adaptation across Layers
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+s\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{N_e}\pi_j(x)\,B_j\Big)A_{g(l)}x,\ \ \pi(x)=\mathrm{softmax}\big(R\,A_{g(l)}x\big),\ A_{g(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ shared by a group of stride\_A layers},\ B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ shared by all layers}
methods.structure: low-rank update with cross-layer sharing: locally shared down-projections A and a global pool of up-projection experts B mixed by a data-dependent router
methods.mergeable_reason: The B mixture depends on the input at runtime, so there is no fixed Delta W to merge.
methods.identity_at_init: B experts zero-initialized (A Kaiming) in PEFT, so the adapter output is zero at start.
methods.key_idea: Share adapter matrices across layers and route among them, so the freed budget buys a much higher rank than per-layer LoRA.
methods.results_note: Paper reports 82.8 average on commonsense reasoning with LLaMA3-8B using 1.2M parameters versus 80.8 for LoRA with 56M.

relations.note: Same A/B factorization, but A and B are shared across layers and B is routed.
Both share parameters globally across layers to cut cost.

methods.name: LN Tuning
methods.paper_title: Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{LN}(x)=\gamma\odot\frac{x-\mu(x)}{\sigma(x)}+\beta,\ \ \text{only } \gamma,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ of (attention-block) LayerNorms trained}
methods.structure: per-channel affine rescaling/shift of normalized activations (diagonal), applied by training existing LayerNorm parameters
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing parameters change; the architecture is untouched.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivially identity: starts from the pretrained gamma and beta.
methods.key_idea: Turning an LLM into a multimodal LLM is largely a domain-adaptation problem that LayerNorm parameters alone can absorb.
methods.results_note: Paper reports, on 13B MLLMs, about 20% better average performance than LoRA across five multimodal benchmarks with 41.9% fewer trainable parameters and 17.6% less GPU memory.

relations.note: Both tune tiny existing parameter subsets (norms vs biases).
Both are diagonal per-channel rescalings.

methods.name: LoHa
methods.paper_title: FedPara: Low-Rank Hadamard Product for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2),\ \ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}
methods.locus: linear and Conv1d/Conv2d layers (popular for diffusion models via LyCORIS)
methods.structure: Hadamard product of two rank-r matrices, \operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le r^2
methods.mergeable_reason: The Hadamard product is a fixed dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized (PEFT: B_2 = 0; others Kaiming).
methods.key_idea: A Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices reaches rank r^2 with 2x LoRA's parameters.
methods.results_note: FedPara reports accuracy comparable to the original model with 3-10x lower communication cost in federated learning; LoHa was popularized for diffusion fine-tuning by LyCORIS (ICLR 2024).

relations.note: Squared-rank capacity from two LoRA-style factors combined multiplicatively.
Sibling LyCORIS method using a Kronecker instead of Hadamard product.
HiRA uses W_0 itself as the second Hadamard factor.

methods.name: LoKr
methods.paper_title: Navigating Text-To-Image Customization: From LyCORIS Fine-Tuning to Model Evaluation
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=C\otimes(BA),\ \ C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{p}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times\frac{d_{in}}{q}} \ \ (C \text{ also low-rank if decompose\_both})
methods.structure: Kronecker product of a small dense factor and a low-rank factor, \operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le\operatorname{rank}(C)\cdot r
methods.mergeable_reason: The Kronecker product is a fixed dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT zero-initializes the left Kronecker factor C (w1), so Delta W = 0.
methods.key_idea: Kronecker structure gives high-rank, block-repetitive updates with very few parameters.
methods.results_note: The LyCORIS paper provides a systematic evaluation framework for text-to-image customization comparing LoRA, LoHa, LoKr and native fine-tuning.

relations.note: Kronecker-product adapters (KronA) with an extra low-rank factor.
Sibling LyCORIS method (Hadamard instead of Kronecker).

methods.name: MiSS (formerly Bone)
methods.full_name: Matrix Shard Sharing (successor of Block-Affine Adaptation, Bone)
methods.paper_title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\mathrm{expand}(D),\ \ \Delta W\,x=D\,S(x),\ S(x)_j=\sum_{t\in\text{shard } j}x_t,\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\ \text{i.e. } \Delta W=D\,(I_r\otimes\mathbf{1}^\top_{d_{in}/r})
methods.structure: shard sharing: one d_{out}\times r matrix whose columns are replicated across the d_{in}/r input shards (rank \le r); 'bat' mode adds a nonlinear block-affine interaction with W_0
methods.mergeable_reason: expand(D) is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.key_idea: A single small matrix shared across input shards keeps LoRA-like expressivity with lower compute, memory and no expensive initialization.
methods.results_note: Paper reports Llama2-7B GSM8K 48.16 vs 40.75 for LoRA and MATH 8.58 vs 5.22.

relations.note: Single-matrix alternative with O(d_out r) parameters and cheaper FLOPs.
MiSS is the revised version of Bone (Block-Affine Adaptation), which PEFT removed in favor of MiSS.

methods.name: MPT
methods.paper_title: Multitask Prompt Tuning Enables Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: P_k=P^*\odot(u_kv_k^\top),\ \ P^*\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d} \text{ shared (distilled from source tasks)},\ u_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell},v_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d};\ \text{input}=[P_k;E(x)]
methods.structure: soft prompt = Hadamard product of a shared prompt matrix and a task-specific rank-one matrix
methods.mergeable_reason: Prompt tokens extend the input sequence; they are not a weight change.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity (adds tokens); target prompts initialized from the distilled shared source prompt.
methods.key_idea: Distill many source-task prompts into one shared prompt and adapt it to each target task with a cheap multiplicative rank-one update.
methods.results_note: Paper reports SuperGLUE average 74.1 vs 57.8 for vanilla prompt tuning while tuning 0.035% task-specific parameters.

relations.note: Soft prompt with multitask-shared structure.
Same Hadamard-with-low-rank idea applied to a prompt matrix instead of a weight.

methods.name: OFT
methods.paper_title: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0R^\top,\ \ R=\mathrm{blockdiag}(R_1,\dots,R_n)\in O(d_{in}),\ R_i=(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i^\top=-Q_i\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b},\ n=d_{in}/b;\ \text{COFT: }\|Q\|\le\epsilon
methods.locus: linear and Conv2d layers (rotation of each neuron's input-weight vector)
methods.structure: block-diagonal orthogonal R\in O(d_{in}) (Cayley-parameterized) multiplying W_0, preserving hyperspherical energy (pairwise angles between neurons)
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 R^T is a dense matrix that replaces W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0, so R = I.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune by rotating neurons rather than adding to them, which provably preserves the pairwise angular structure of pretrained weights.
methods.results_note: Paper reports better generation quality and faster convergence than existing methods on subject-driven and controllable text-to-image generation.

relations.note: BOFT with a single butterfly factor.
OFTv2 is the scalable input-centric reformulation implemented in PEFT >= 0.16.
Alternative orthogonal parameterization.

methods.name: OFTv2
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable (input-centric OFT with Cayley-Neumann)
methods.paper_title: Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0\,(R^\top x),\ \ R_i=(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1}\approx(I+Q_i)\sum_{k=0}^{K}Q_i^{k},\ Q_i^\top=-Q_i
methods.locus: linear layers, including quantized base layers (QOFT)
methods.structure: block-diagonal orthogonal rotation applied to activations (matrix-vector) instead of weights (matrix-matrix), with a truncated Neumann series replacing the Cayley inverse
methods.mergeable_reason: The rotation can still be folded into W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0, so R = I.
methods.key_idea: Make OFT input-centric and replace the matrix inverse with a Neumann series to cut OFT's compute and memory to LoRA-like levels.
methods.results_note: Paper reports up to 10x faster training and 3x lower GPU memory than OFT without performance loss, and better stability/efficiency than QLoRA on quantized models.

relations.note: Same orthogonal parameterization, scalable computation.
QOFT targets quantized base models like QLoRA.

methods.name: OSF
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning (adaptive-SVD constrained full fine-tuning)
methods.paper_title: Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex:
W_0=U_{hi}\Sigma_{hi}V_{hi}^	op+U_{lo}\Sigma_{lo}V_{lo}^	op;\ U_{hi},\Sigma_{hi},V_{hi} 	ext{ frozen};\ U_{lo},\Sigma_{lo},V_{lo} 	ext{ trained with } 
abla_{proj}=
abla-U_{hi}U_{hi}^	op
abla\,V_{hi}V_{hi}^	op
methods.structure: SVD split of W_0: top singular subspace (important for prior tasks) frozen; minor singular components trained with gradients projected orthogonally to the frozen subspace
methods.mergeable_reason: The frozen and trained SVD components recombine into one dense W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trainable components initialized from W_0's own SVD, so W = W_0 at init.
methods.key_idea: For continual learning, update only directions orthogonal to the dominant singular subspaces of earlier tasks, giving full-rank-capacity updates with little forgetting.
methods.results_note: Paper reports 71.3 vs 69.6 (O-LoRA) on the 15-task T5-Large benchmark and 48.4 vs 41.3 on TRACE with LLaMA-2 7B.

relations.note: Both use orthogonality to prior-task subspaces; OSF does it within full-rank SVD components.
Both train minor singular components of W_0.

methods.name: P-Tuning
methods.paper_title: GPT Understands, Too
methods.formula_latex: \text{input}=[\,\dots,h_1,\dots,h_\ell,\dots,E(x),\dots],\ \ h_{1:\ell}=f_\phi(p_{1:\ell}),\ f_\phi\in\{\text{LSTM},\text{MLP}\},\ p_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ trained}
methods.structure: continuous virtual tokens produced by a trainable reparameterizing encoder (LSTM/MLP) and inserted into the input embeddings
methods.mergeable_reason: Virtual tokens extend the input sequence.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity (adds tokens).
methods.key_idea: Learn continuous prompt embeddings through a small prompt encoder, which stabilizes optimization compared with free prompt vectors.

relations.note: Same input-level soft prompt, but reparameterized through an encoder.
Input-only vs every-layer prompts.

methods.name: PEANuT
methods.full_name: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
methods.paper_title: PEANuT: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+f(W_0;\theta),\ \ f(W_0;\theta)=\sigma(W_0\Theta_1)\,\Theta_2,\ \Theta_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\ \Theta_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \ (\text{optional depth: extra } r\times r \text{ nonlinear layers})
methods.structure: nonlinear weight-conditioned update: a small MLP applied to the rows of W_0 produces \Delta W (rank \le r)
methods.mergeable_reason: f(W_0) is computed once after training and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Output projection Theta_2 (B) zero-initialized.
methods.key_idea: Generate the update as a nonlinear function of the frozen weight itself instead of a weight-agnostic linear factorization.
methods.results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over strong PEFT baselines on four benchmarks spanning 20+ NLP and vision datasets at comparable or fewer parameters.

relations.note: With identity activation and Theta_1 absorbing W_0, the update is a rank-r linear map like LoRA (paper shows >= expressivity).
Both condition the update on W_0 (nonlinear MLP vs Hadamard).

methods.name: Polytropon (Poly)
methods.full_name: Polytropon: modular skill inventory with task-level routing
methods.paper_title: Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_\tau=\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{S}\hat z_{\tau j}B_j\Big)\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{S}\hat z_{\tau j}A_j\Big),\ \ \hat z_{\tau j}=\frac{z_{\tau j}}{\sum_k z_{\tau k}},\ z_{\tau}\sim\mathrm{RelaxedBernoulli}(\mathrm{logits}_\tau)
methods.locus: LoRA-style adapters on linear layers, selected per task id
methods.structure: task-level routing over an inventory of S LoRA skills; each task's adapter is the normalized average of its active skills' parameters
methods.mergeable_reason: For a fixed task id the averaged adapter is a fixed low-rank update that could be merged; in multitask use the routing varies per task.
methods.identity_at_init: Skill B matrices zero-initialized in PEFT; routing logits ~U(-1e-3, 1e-3).
methods.key_idea: Tasks share a small inventory of latent skills (adapters); learn which skills each task uses so knowledge recombines across tasks.
methods.results_note: Paper reports improved few-shot generalization on CrossFit (NLP) and sample efficiency on BabyAI over non-modular baselines.

relations.note: MHR with a single routing head equals Poly.
Each skill is a LoRA adapter.

methods.name: MHR
methods.paper_title: Multi-Head Adapter Routing for Cross-Task Generalization
methods.formula_latex: A^{(\tau)}=\mathrm{concat}_{h=1}^{H}\Big(\sum_{j}\hat z^{(h)}_{\tau j}A^{(h)}_j\Big),\ B^{(\tau)} \text{ analogously},\ \Delta W_\tau=B^{(\tau)}A^{(\tau)}
methods.locus: LoRA-style adapters on linear layers, routed per task
methods.structure: adapters split into H disjoint parameter blocks, each with its own task-to-skill routing, giving finer-grained combinations than Poly
methods.mergeable_reason: For a known task the routed adapter is a fixed low-rank update; across tasks it varies.
methods.identity_at_init: Skill B matrices zero-initialized in PEFT.
methods.key_idea: Route subsets of adapter parameters (heads) rather than whole adapters to increase the expressivity of skill combination.
methods.results_note: Paper reports MHR outperforming Poly in few-shot cross-task generalization.

relations.note: H = 1 recovers Poly.
Both reuse a library of LoRAs for cross-task generalization.

methods.name: Prefix Tuning
methods.paper_title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
methods.formula_latex: \forall l:\ K_l=[P^{(l)}_K;\,W_kX],\ V_l=[P^{(l)}_V;\,W_vX],\ P^{(l)}_K,P^{(l)}_V\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d};\ \ P=\mathrm{MLP}_\theta(P') \text{ during training (prefix\_projection)}
methods.structure: learned key/value vectors prepended at every attention layer (served as past_key_values)
methods.mergeable_reason: Extra attended KV states are not a weight change.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity with random init; PEFT's init_weights='zero' (v0.19) makes the prefix activations zero, approximately a no-op.
methods.key_idea: Steer a frozen LM by learning virtual tokens that every layer can attend to.
methods.results_note: Paper reports comparable performance to fine-tuning in full-data table-to-text and summarization with 0.1% of parameters, and better results in low-data settings.

relations.note: Prompt tuning is the input-layer-only special case.
Same KV-prefix mechanism trained by self-study distillation.

methods.name: Prompt Tuning
methods.paper_title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{input}=[P;\,E(x)],\ \ P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d} \text{ trained},\ \text{model frozen}
methods.structure: learned soft-token embeddings prepended to the input
methods.mergeable_reason: Soft tokens extend the input; nothing to fold into weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity (adds tokens); initialized randomly, from text (vocab embeddings), or by random discrete vocab sampling (PEFT >= 0.18).
methods.key_idea: With large enough models, a few learned input embeddings match full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Paper reports prompt tuning closing the gap to model tuning as T5 scales past billions of parameters.

relations.note: Prefix tuning restricted to the input layer.
P-tuning reparameterizes the prompt through an encoder.

methods.name: PSOFT
methods.full_name: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
methods.paper_title: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_0=AB+W_{res}\ (AB=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top);\ \ W=A\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)\,R\,\mathrm{diag}(\beta)\,B+W_{res}=W_0+A\big(\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)R\,\mathrm{diag}(\beta)-I_r\big)B,\ R\in O(r) \text{ (Cayley)}
methods.structure: orthogonal transform R\in O(r) acting inside the rank-r principal singular subspace of W_0, with optional diagonal relaxations of orthogonality
methods.mergeable_reason: The additive form A(R' - I)B is a fixed low-rank update.
methods.identity_at_init: R = I and alpha = beta = 1 at init, so W = W_0.
methods.key_idea: Confine orthogonal fine-tuning to the low-rank principal subspace, getting OFT's geometry preservation at LoRA-like cost.

relations.note: Orthogonal transformation, restricted to an r-dim principal subspace.
Uses the principal SVD subspace of W_0 like PiSSA.
Implemented as the additive low-rank update A(R - I)B.

methods.name: PVeRA
methods.paper_title: PVeRA: Probabilistic Vector-Based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: (\mu,\sigma)=\Lambda_dAx,\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{2r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen shared};\ z=\mu+\sigma\odot\epsilon,\ \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I);\ h=W_0x+\Lambda_bBz;\ \ \mathcal{L}\mathrel{+}=\beta\,D_{KL}\big(\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(0,I)\big)
methods.structure: VeRA with a reparameterized Gaussian latent in the shared random bottleneck; frozen shared random bases with trainable diagonal scalings
methods.mergeable_reason: With z = mu at inference the adapter is a fixed linear map and can be merged; sampling for Monte Carlo uncertainty (sample_at_inference) cannot.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (d initialized to 0.1), so the update is zero.
methods.key_idea: Learn a distribution over VeRA's latent adaptation, improving accuracy and enabling Monte Carlo confidence estimates.
methods.results_note: Paper reports VTAB-1k average 71.4 vs 69.9 for VeRA, 70.5 for LoRA and 71.0 for DoRA.

relations.note: Same frozen shared random bases; adds a probabilistic latent.
Both make low-rank adapters Bayesian/stochastic.

methods.name: RandLoRA
methods.full_name: RandLoRA: full-rank PEFT via scaled random bases
methods.paper_title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\sum_{j=1}^{n}B_j\Lambda_jA\,\Gamma_j,\ \ B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen random (shared)},\ \Lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ \Gamma_j \text{ trainable diagonal},\ n=\lceil\min(d_{in},d_{out})/r\rceil
methods.structure: sum of n frozen random rank-r bases with trainable diagonal scalings on both sides, reaching full rank; parameter count grows as the basis rank shrinks
methods.mergeable_reason: The scaled sum of bases is a fixed dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Lambda_j = 0 (Gamma_j = 1/n) in PEFT, so Delta W = 0.
methods.key_idea: Separate parameter count from rank: combine many frozen random low-rank bases with learned diagonal scalings to get full-rank updates cheaply.
methods.results_note: Paper reports RandLoRA overtaking LoRA as the parameter budget grows on vision (DinoV2, CLIP), vision-language and commonsense reasoning (e.g. LLaMA3-8B).

relations.note: VeRA is a single-basis special case with one scaling per side.
Full-rank alternative at similar budgets.

methods.name: RoAd
methods.paper_title: 3-in-1: 2D Rotary Adaptation for Efficient Finetuning, Efficient Batching and Composability
methods.formula_latex: W=RW_0,\ \ R=\mathrm{blockdiag}_i\Big(\alpha_i\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta_i&-\sin\theta_i\\\sin\theta_i&\cos\theta_i\end{bmatrix}\Big) \text{ over output pairs};\ \ h=r_1\odot(W_0x)+r_2\odot\widehat{(W_0x)}
methods.locus: linear layers (outputs); works with bitsandbytes-quantized bases
methods.structure: block-diagonal 2x2 scaled rotations applied to pairs of output dimensions, implemented element-wise
methods.mergeable_reason: R W_0 is a dense matrix; unmerged it is cheap element-wise ops enabling mixed-adapter batches.
methods.identity_at_init: theta = 0 and alpha = 1, so R = I.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning mostly rotates representations, so learn tiny 2D rotations that are element-wise (batchable across adapters) and composable.
methods.results_note: Paper reports matching or beating full fine-tuning on GLUE with <0.1% trainable parameters and 2x LoRA's throughput in heterogeneous multi-adapter batches.

relations.note: With theta = 0 RoAd reduces to per-channel scaling like (IA)^3.
Both are orthogonal-style multiplicative updates; RoAd uses 2x2 blocks on the output side.

methods.name: ShadowPEFT
methods.paper_title: ShadowPEFT: Shadow Network for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.locus: every decoder block input (whole-block wrapper) plus a parallel small shadow backbone
methods.structure: parallel shadow network whose state is injected into each block input through a rank-r bottleneck of the base-shadow discrepancy and advanced by gated residual MLP updates
methods.mergeable_reason: The adaptation is an input-dependent trajectory through a separate network, not a weight delta (PEFT raises on merge).
methods.identity_at_init: W_up zero-initialized, so the injection is a no-op at start.
methods.key_idea: Share adaptation across layers through a small, detachable, pretrainable shadow model that runs alongside the frozen backbone.
methods.results_note: Paper reports outperforming LoRA and DoRA at comparable budgets (~29M params on Qwen3-8B) on MMLU, GSM8K and SQuAD v2, with the best OOD average.

relations.note: Inserted modules, but in a parallel stateful network rather than per-layer bottlenecks.
Same trainable-parameter range with layer-shared adaptation.

methods.name: SHiRA
methods.paper_title: Sparse High Rank Adapters
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+M\odot S,\ \ M\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ fixed},\ \|M\|_0=r(d_{in}+d_{out}),\ S \text{ trained on the support of } M
methods.structure: sparse coordinate mask on W_0 (random, magnitude, gradient, SNIP or structured), giving a sparse but high-rank update
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing entries change; the sparse delta is scattered into W_0 (fast switching via sparse indices).
methods.key_idea: Directly fine-tune a tiny sparse subset of existing weights: high-rank, cheap to switch, and less interference when fusing adapters.
methods.results_note: Paper reports HPSv2 31.2 vs 24.7 for LoRA on a style task, +2.7% over LoRA on LLaMA-7B commonsense, and 5-16x faster adapter loading than LoRA fusing.

relations.note: Both train a fixed sparse support of W_0; Super-Tuning picks it by magnitude.
Same parameter count as LoRA but sparse/high-rank.

methods.name: Super-Tuning (Super / Supra)
methods.full_name: Super-Tuning: sparse fine-tuning from activation-aware pruning saliency
methods.paper_title: Super-Tuning: From Activation-Aware Pruning to Sparse Fine-Tuning
methods.hf_peft_config: SupertuningConfig (r=None: Super; r>0: Supra hybrid; select_top=False: bottom-k)
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+M\odot U\ \big(+\,\gamma BA \text{ in Supra}\big),\ \ M=\mathrm{TopK}\ \text{or}\ \mathrm{BottomK}\big(|W_0|\big) \text{ (paper also: } |W_{ij}|\,\|X_{j}\|_2\text{)}
methods.structure: sparse coordinate mask chosen data-free by weight magnitude (or Wanda-style saliency in the paper); Supra = sparse-plus-low-rank
methods.mergeable_reason: Sparse and low-rank deltas are fixed matrices that add into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Sparse values U = 0 and LoRA B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Reuse pruning saliency to choose an unrestricted-rank sparse trainable support at a fixed budget, optionally adding a low-rank part.
methods.results_note: Paper reports Supra beating LoRA on Math17K (Llama-3.2-1B 62.23 vs 61.07; Meta-Llama-3-8B 79.12 vs 73.17).

relations.note: Sparse fixed-support fine-tuning with a different mask criterion.
Supra adds a LoRA term to the sparse update.

methods.name: TinyLoRA
methods.paper_title: Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+U_r\Sigma_r\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{u}v_iP_i\Big)V_r^\top,\ \ U_r,\Sigma_r,V_r \text{ from truncated SVD of } W_0 \text{ (frozen)},\ P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r} \text{ fixed random},\ v\in\mathbb{R}^{u} \text{ trained, optionally tied across modules}
methods.trainable_params: u \text{ per module, or } u \text{ for the whole model with full weight tying}
methods.structure: LoRA-XS core R=\sum_i v_iP_i confined to a u-dimensional random subspace of r\times r matrices in the top-r singular frame of W_0
methods.mergeable_reason: The update is a fixed rank-r matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: v ~ U(-0.02, 0.02) in PEFT, so near- but not exactly identity.
methods.key_idea: With RL, reasoning can be unlocked by a handful of parameters projected through fixed random tensors into the principal singular frame.
methods.results_note: Paper reports Qwen2.5-8B reaching 91% on GSM8K with 13 trained parameters under RL, and RL vastly outperforming SFT at tiny budgets.

relations.note: Replaces LoRA-XS's trainable r x r core with a random projection of a tiny vector.
Both project a tiny global vector into LoRA-style parameters.

methods.name: Trainable Tokens
methods.formula_latex: E=E_0+\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}e_t\,\delta_t^\top,\ \ \delta_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ trained only for selected token ids } \mathcal{T}
methods.locus: rows of the input embedding (and tied LM head)
methods.structure: sparse row mask on the embedding matrix
methods.mergeable_reason: Updated rows are written back into the embedding matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: New row values initialized to the existing token embeddings (no-op).
methods.key_idea: Train only the embeddings of new or special tokens (e.g. reasoning tokens) without full-embedding fine-tuning or a LoRA on the embedding.
methods.results_note: PEFT docs report about 4 GiB VRAM saved on gemma-2-2b versus fully fine-tuning the embedding matrix.

relations.note: Both are sparse selective updates of existing parameters (rows vs entries).
Usable together with LoRA through trainable_token_indices.

methods.name: Uni-LoRA
methods.full_name: Uni-LoRA: one vector is all you need
methods.paper_title: Uni-LoRA: One Vector is All You Need
methods.formula_latex: \theta_D=P\,\theta_d,\ \ \theta_D=\mathrm{vec}\{(A_\ell,B_\ell)\}_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{D},\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times d} \text{ fixed: one-hot rows (uniform random slot), columns scaled by } 1/\sqrt{n_j};\ W_\ell=W_{0,\ell}+B_\ell A_\ell
methods.structure: global random isometric projection from one d-dim vector to all LoRA parameters of the model (random parameter tying across layers)
methods.mergeable_reason: Each layer's B_l A_l is fixed after training.
methods.identity_at_init: theta_d ~ U(-0.02, 0.02): both A and B are small but nonzero, so not an exact no-op.
methods.key_idea: All parameter-sharing LoRA variants are projections of LoRA's parameter space; a single global, isometric projection gives extreme efficiency.
methods.results_note: Paper reports Gemma-7B instruction tuning comparable to LoRA with 0.52M parameters (0.0061% of the model, 0.26% of LoRA).

relations.note: VeRA is a particular (layer-wise, structured) projection theta_D = P theta_d.
VB-LoRA is another projection choice in the same framework.
Both train a tiny vector projected into low-rank adapters.

methods.name: VB-LoRA
methods.paper_title: VB-LoRA: Extreme Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning with Vector Banks
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=BA,\ \text{each length-}b \text{ sub-vector } u \text{ of } A,B:\ u=\sum_{s=1}^{h}w_s(\sigma_u)\,\alpha_s,\ w(\sigma)=\mathrm{softmax}(\mathrm{TopK}(\sigma,k)),\ \{\alpha_s\}_{s=1}^{h}\subset\mathbb{R}^{b} \text{ shared bank}
methods.trainable_params: hb+h\cdot\#\text{sub-vectors (logits) in training; stored: } hb+3\cdot\#\text{sub-vectors for } k=2
methods.structure: LoRA factors assembled from a global vector bank by top-k sparse admixtures
methods.mergeable_reason: BA is fixed after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: bank ~U(-0.02, 0.02) and logits ~N(0, 0.1^2), so BA is small but nonzero.
methods.key_idea: Share a tiny global bank of vectors from which every LoRA sub-vector is mixed, pushing parameter sharing across all layers and modules.
methods.results_note: Paper reports VB-LoRA using only 0.4% of LoRA's stored parameters on Llama2-13B while achieving better results.

relations.note: A particular projection choice within Uni-LoRA's framework.

methods.name: VeRA
methods.paper_title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+\Lambda_bB\Lambda_dAx,\ \ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ frozen random, shared across layers},\ \Lambda_d=\mathrm{diag}(d),\Lambda_b=\mathrm{diag}(b) \text{ trained}
methods.locus: linear layers (shared A/B sliced to each layer's shape)
methods.structure: frozen shared random low-rank bases with trainable diagonal scalings on both sides
methods.mergeable_reason: Lambda_b B Lambda_d A is a fixed low-rank matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (d = 0.1), so the update is zero.
methods.key_idea: Random projections are good enough as LoRA bases; only learn per-layer scaling vectors.
methods.results_note: Paper reports matching LoRA with 10x fewer trainable parameters on GLUE, E2E and instruction tuning.

relations.note: Fixes LoRA's A, B to shared random matrices and learns diagonal scalings.
Single-basis special case of RandLoRA.
A structured projection in Uni-LoRA's theta_D = P theta_d view.

methods.name: WaveFT
methods.paper_title: Exploring Sparsity for Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning Using Wavelets
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\lambda\,\mathrm{IDWT}(C),\ \ C\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ sparse with } p \text{ trainable coefficients at fixed random locations}
methods.locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT); designed for SDXL personalization
methods.structure: inverse 2D discrete wavelet transform of a sparse coefficient matrix (high-rank, spatially localized update)
methods.mergeable_reason: IDWT(C) is computed once and added to W_0.
methods.key_idea: Learn a few wavelet coefficients of the update, giving parameter counts far below LoRA's rank-1 minimum with fine-grained control.
methods.results_note: Paper reports SDXL DreamBooth DINO 0.495 vs 0.463 for LoRA at equal parameter count and higher output diversity.

relations.note: Sparse coefficients in a wavelet rather than Fourier basis.
Sparse update, but sparse in a transform domain rather than in W itself.

methods.name: X-LoRA
methods.paper_title: X-LoRA: Mixture of Low-Rank Adapter Experts, a Flexible Framework for Large Language Models with Applications in Protein Mechanics and Molecular Design
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_i(x)\,\tfrac{\alpha_i}{r_i}B_iA_ix,\ \ \lambda=\mathrm{softmax}/\mathrm{top}\text{-}k\big(g_\phi(\text{hidden states of a first scaling pass})\big) \text{ per token (and per layer)}
methods.trainable_params: |\phi| \ (\text{scaling head; LoRA experts frozen unless use\_trainable\_adapters})
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted layers; scalings predicted from hidden states
methods.structure: dense token-level gating of a set of pretrained LoRA experts by a learned scaling head (two forward passes)
methods.mergeable_reason: Mixing weights depend on each token's hidden state.
methods.identity_at_init: Not a no-op: pretrained LoRA experts are mixed from the start.
methods.key_idea: Reuse several domain LoRAs as experts and learn a small head that mixes them token by token, layer by layer.

relations.note: Mixes multiple trained LoRA adapters.
Arrow routes LoRAs training-free; X-LoRA trains a gating head.

methods.name: DoRA
methods.paper_title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_{i,:}=m_i\,\frac{(W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)_{i,:}}{\|(W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)_{i,:}\|_2},\ \ m\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ trained (init } m_i=\|(W_0)_{i,:}\|_2),\ B,A \text{ as LoRA}
methods.structure: magnitude-direction decomposition: learned per-output norm times the normalized (W_0 + low-rank) direction (the paper's 'column-wise' norm in its transposed convention)
methods.mergeable_reason: After training m and the normalized direction combine into one dense weight (merging recommended to remove the overhead).
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 and m = row norms of W_0, so W = W_0.
methods.key_idea: Full fine-tuning changes magnitude and direction differently; let LoRA handle direction and a separate vector handle magnitude.
methods.results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over LoRA on commonsense reasoning (LLaMA family), visual instruction tuning and image/video-text understanding.

relations.note: LoRA updates the direction component.
DeLoRA normalizes the update instead of the full weight.

methods.name: rsLoRA
methods.paper_title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r}}BA \quad(\text{instead of } \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)
methods.structure: LoRA with rank-dependent scale 1/sqrt(r), which keeps activations and gradients O(1) as r grows
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the scalar scale changes; the update is still BA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA.
methods.key_idea: The alpha/r scaling makes high-rank LoRA learn too slowly (gradient collapse); alpha/sqrt(r) is the rank-stable choice.
methods.results_note: Paper shows that with alpha/sqrt(r), fine-tuning performance keeps improving as rank increases, unlike standard LoRA scaling.

relations.note: Changes only the scaling factor.
Both fix LoRA's training dynamics through scaling (of output vs learning rates).

methods.name: PiSSA
methods.full_name: Principal Singular values and Singular vectors Adaptation
methods.paper_title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^\top;\ B=U_{[:,:r]}\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2},\ A=\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2}V_{[:,:r]}^\top,\ W^{res}=U_{[:,r:]}\Sigma_{[r:]}V_{[:,r:]}^\top \text{ frozen};\ W=W^{res}+BA
methods.locus: same as LoRA (also reduces quantization error when W^res is quantized)
methods.structure: LoRA whose factors are initialized to the principal rank-r SVD component of W_0, with the residual frozen
methods.mergeable_reason: W^res + BA is a dense weight; PEFT can convert to a standard LoRA delta relative to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W^res + BA = W_0 at init (base weight is modified to the residual).
methods.key_idea: Train the principal components and freeze the noise-like residual, which converges faster and better than random LoRA init.
methods.results_note: Paper reports Mistral-7B GSM8K 72.86% with PiSSA vs 67.7% with LoRA.

relations.note: Same architecture, SVD-based initialization.
MiCA uses the minor instead of principal singular directions.

methods.name: OLoRA
methods.paper_title: OLoRA: Orthonormal Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=QR_{qr};\ B=Q_{[:,:r]},\ A=(R_{qr})_{[:r,:]};\ W_0\leftarrow W_0-s\,BA \text{ (frozen)};\ W=W_0-sB_0A_0+sBA
methods.structure: LoRA initialized from the QR decomposition of W_0 (orthonormal B), with the base weight translated so the model is unchanged
methods.mergeable_reason: Standard low-rank delta relative to the translated base.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: base weight is shifted by -sBA at init.
methods.key_idea: An orthonormal basis from W_0's QR decomposition gives a better-conditioned starting point and faster convergence.
methods.results_note: Paper reports higher final performance than LoRA in 53 of 60 model-task-rank combinations.

relations.note: Weight-derived initialization via QR rather than SVD.

methods.name: LoftQ
methods.paper_title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \text{for } t=1..T:\ Q_t=q_N\big(W_0-B_{t-1}A_{t-1}\big),\ \ B_tA_t=\mathrm{SVD}_r\big(W_0-Q_t\big);\ \ W=Q_T+BA,\ Q_T \text{ frozen (quantized)}

methods.structure: LoRA initialized jointly with the quantized backbone so that Q + BA approximates W_0 (alternating quantization and low-rank SVD)
methods.mergeable_reason: The LoRA can be merged only into a dequantized (higher-precision) copy of the backbone.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q_T + B_T A_T ~ W_0 (minimizes the quantization residual in Frobenius norm).
methods.key_idea: Choose the LoRA initialization to absorb the quantization error, instead of starting QLoRA from a degraded quantized model.
methods.results_note: Paper reports outperforming QLoRA, especially in 2-bit and mixed 2/4-bit regimes, on NLU, QA, summarization and NLG.

relations.note: Same quantized-backbone + LoRA setting with error-correcting init.
PiSSA also reduces quantization error by quantizing only the residual.

methods.name: EVA
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning via Explained Variance Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: X=USV^\top \text{ (incremental SVD of input activations of the layer)};\ A=V_{[:,:r_\ell]}^\top,\ B=0;\ \xi_i=\frac{\sigma_i^2}{(M-1)\|\sigma\|_1};\ \{r_\ell\} \text{ chosen by top explained variance under } \textstyle\sum_\ell r_\ell=rN,\ r_\ell\le\rho r
methods.structure: LoRA with A initialized to the top right-singular vectors of the layer's input activations, plus data-driven rank redistribution
methods.mergeable_reason: Standard LoRA update.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (exact no-op).
methods.key_idea: Initialize A to the directions of maximal activation variance (which maximizes the expected gradient signal) and give more rank where variance is spread out.
methods.results_note: Paper reports EVA Pareto-dominating competitors across language generation/understanding, image classification and RL with fewer trainable parameters.

relations.note: Both redistribute ranks across layers.
Both use task-data activation statistics to initialize LoRA.

methods.name: CorDA
methods.paper_title: CorDA: Context-Oriented Decomposition Adaptation of Large Language Models for Task-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: C=XX^\top;\ \mathrm{SVD}(W_0C)=U\Sigma V^\top;\ \hat W=U\Sigma(V^\top C^{-1});\ \text{IPM: } B=U_{:,:r}\Sigma_{:r}^{1/2},\ A=\Sigma_{:r}^{1/2}(V^\top C^{-1})_{:r,:};\ \text{KPM: same with the last } r \text{ components; rest frozen}

methods.mergeable_reason: Frozen residual + BA is a dense weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: residual + BA reconstructs W_0 (C^{-1} undoes the covariance orientation).
methods.key_idea: Orient the weight decomposition by task (or knowledge) activation covariance so the adapter captures exactly the directions to learn (IPM) or to leave untouched (KPM).
methods.results_note: Paper reports KPM preserving world knowledge (TriviaQA, NQ, WebQS) while beating LoRA on math, code and instruction following, and IPM surpassing LoRA, DoRA and PiSSA.

relations.note: With C = I, IPM reduces to PiSSA's principal-component initialization.
Both are activation-aware SVD/eigen initializations.

methods.name: Astra
methods.paper_title: Astra: Activation-Space Tail-Eigenvector Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Cov}(Y)=Q\Lambda Q^\top \text{ (output activations on a calibration set)};\ B_0=Q_{tail}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_0=Q_{tail}^\top W_0;\ \ W=(W_0-B_0A_0)+BA
methods.structure: LoRA initialized as the projection of W_0 onto the tail eigenspace of the layer's output-activation covariance, residual frozen
methods.mergeable_reason: Frozen residual + BA is a dense weight.
methods.key_idea: Under-used (tail) activation directions are where task-specific changes fit best, so constrain the adapter to that subspace.
methods.results_note: Paper reports outperforming LoRA variants across 16 benchmarks, with rank-8 Astra surpassing rank-128 LoRA on math reasoning.

relations.note: Activation-covariance-oriented initialization (output-side tail eigenvectors vs input-covariance SVD).
Both target minor/tail directions (activation space vs weight singular space).

methods.name: MiCA
methods.paper_title: MiCA Learns More Knowledge Than LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^\top;\ B=U_{[:,-r:]} \text{ (frozen)},\ A=0 \text{ (trained)};\ W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA
methods.structure: update confined to the column space of the r minor left-singular vectors of W_0 (B fixed, only A learned)
methods.mergeable_reason: BA is a fixed low-rank update.
methods.identity_at_init: A = 0 (exact no-op without modifying the base weight).
methods.key_idea: Write new knowledge into the least-used singular directions of the pretrained weight to absorb more and interfere less.
methods.results_note: Paper reports up to 5.9x better knowledge acquisition than LoRA, e.g. 61.33% vs 58.28% on BLOGS-MC with Llama-2-7B.

relations.note: Uses minor instead of principal singular directions.
Both freeze one LoRA factor (MiCA freezes B, LoRA-FA freezes A).
Both exploit minor singular components.

methods.name: LoRA-GA
methods.paper_title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
methods.formula_latex: G=\nabla_{W_0}\mathcal{L}\approx USV^\top \text{ (sampled batches)};\ A_0=c\,V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\ B_0=c\,U_{[:,r+1:2r]};\ W=(W_0-\eta B_0A_0)+\eta BA
methods.structure: LoRA initialized from the SVD of an estimated full-model gradient so the first low-rank step best approximates the full fine-tuning step, with base weight offset
methods.mergeable_reason: Offset base + BA is a dense weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: base weight is shifted by -eta B_0 A_0; scale c chosen for rank-stable forward/backward ('stable' scaling).
methods.key_idea: Align the initial LoRA gradient with the full fine-tuning gradient to converge 2-4x faster.
methods.results_note: Paper reports +5.69% over LoRA on a GLUE subset with T5-Base and +11.52% on GSM8K and +5.05% on HumanEval with Llama 2-7B, converging 2-4x faster.

relations.note: Data/gradient-aware rather than weight-only SVD initialization.
Both use gradient SVD to pick low-rank subspaces.

methods.name: KaSA
methods.paper_title: KaSA: Knowledge-Aware Singular-Value Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(kasa_config=KasaConfig(beta, gamma)); add LoraModel._get_kasa_loss to the loss
methods.formula_latex: W_{world}=U_{[:,:m-r]}\Sigma_{[:m-r]}V_{[:,:m-r]}^\top \text{ (r minor components of } W_0 \text{ removed)};\ W=W_{world}+\eta\,\Delta U\,\Delta\Sigma\,\Delta V^\top;\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\|\Delta\Sigma\|_F^2+\gamma\big(\|\Delta U^\top\Delta U-I\|_F+\|\Delta V^\top\Delta V-I\|_F\big)
methods.structure: SVD-form low-rank update with a learnable diagonal of singular values on top of a base weight truncated of its r smallest singular components
methods.mergeable_reason: The SVD-form update merges into the (truncated) base weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an exact identity: the base weight is destructively truncated at injection (unload does not restore it); the adapter itself starts as a no-op.
methods.key_idea: Drop noisy long-tail knowledge from W_0 and let learnable singular values activate the knowledge relevant to the task.
methods.results_note: Paper reports beating full fine-tuning in 13 of 14 GLUE scenarios with 0.24% trainable parameters and 84.6% average commonsense accuracy on LLaMA3-8B.

relations.note: Same SVD-form update with orthogonality regularization; KaSA also truncates W_0.
Both act on the minor singular components of W_0 (KaSA removes them).

methods.name: aLoRA
methods.paper_title: Activated LoRA: Fine-tuned LLMs for Intrinsics
methods.formula_latex: h_t=\begin{cases}W_0x_t,& t<t_{inv}\\(W_0+BA)\,x_t,& t\ge t_{inv}\end{cases}\quad\text{for } W\in\{W_q,W_k,W_v\}
methods.locus: attention projections of causal LMs, applied only to tokens at/after the invocation sequence
methods.structure: token-position-gated low-rank update: identity before the invocation token, LoRA after it, so prefix KV caches equal the base model's
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is applied selectively by token position, so it cannot be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA.
methods.key_idea: Activate the adapter only after an invocation string, so the base model's KV cache can be reused and adapters can be switched in mid-conversation for free.
methods.results_note: Paper reports 2-7x faster adapter generation even for 250-token prompts and over 20x on long prompts, with no consistent accuracy difference from LoRA.

relations.note: Same low-rank update, gated by token position.
Both condition adapter use on tokens; aLoRA uses a hard positional switch.

methods.name: QA-LoRA
methods.paper_title: QA-LoRA: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \tilde W=\alpha\odot\Big\lfloor\frac{W_0-\beta}{\alpha}\Big\rceil+\beta \text{ (group-wise INT-}k);\ h=\tilde Wx+s\,BA\,\mathrm{pool}_g(x),\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}/g};\ \text{merge: } \beta'=\beta-s\,(BA)\oslash\alpha

methods.structure: LoRA on group-average-pooled inputs, so the update is constant within each quantization group
methods.mergeable_reason: The group-constant update is absorbed into the quantization zero-points, keeping the merged model in INT4.
methods.key_idea: Balance quantization and adaptation degrees of freedom with group-wise pooling so the fine-tuned model stays quantized after merging.
methods.results_note: Paper reports LLaMA-7B 5-shot MMLU 39.4 vs 36.0 for QLoRA+GPTQ at INT4, with faster inference.

relations.note: QLoRA cannot merge without leaving the quantized format.
Both target quantized-backbone LoRA.

methods.name: MonteCLoRA
methods.paper_title: Robust and Efficient Fine-tuning of LLMs with Bayesian Reparameterization of Low-Rank Adaptation

methods.structure: LoRA whose A factor is treated as a Gaussian mixture (Wishart covariance, Dirichlet weights) estimated by Monte Carlo during training; plain LoRA at inference
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference the sampler is disabled and the adapter is a standard LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA.
methods.key_idea: Treat low-rank parameters as a distribution and average Monte Carlo samples to make LoRA robust to hyperparameters.
methods.results_note: Paper reports up to 62% lower accuracy spread than LoRA across hyperparameters on LLaMA-3.2-3B (and 53% on LLaMA-1-7B commonsense).

relations.note: Bayesian reparameterization of LoRA's A matrix.
Both introduce stochastic latent parameters into low-rank adapters.

methods.name: VeLoRA
methods.full_name: Memory-efficient training with rank-1 sub-token projections
methods.paper_title: VeLoRA: Memory Efficient Training using Rank-1 Sub-Token Projections
methods.formula_latex: \text{fwd: } z=\mathrm{group}_M(x),\ z_p=z\,v \text{ (stored)};\ \text{bwd: } \hat x=\mathrm{ungroup}(z_pv^\top),\ \nabla_A\mathcal{L}=\delta^\top\hat x;\ v\in\mathbb{R}^{M} \text{ fixed (first-batch average)}

methods.name: BD-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Block-Diagonal LoRA for Eliminating Communication Overhead in Tensor Parallel LoRA Serving

methods.name: Arrow
methods.full_name: Arrow routing over a library of LoRAs

methods.paper_title: GenKnowSub: Improving Modularity and Reusability of LLMs through General Knowledge Subtraction

methods.name: LoRA+
methods.full_name: LoRA+ (decoupled learning rates for A and B)
methods.paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models

methods.name: LoRA-FA
methods.paper_title: LoRA-FA: Efficient and Effective Low Rank Representation Fine-tuning

methods.name: Riemannian LoRA
methods.paper_title: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
