methods.mergeable_reason: The trained adapter is a standard LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA (delta regularizes the singular preconditioner).
methods.key_idea: LoRA's factorization is ill-conditioned; precondition each factor by the Gram matrix of the other to follow the geometry of the low-rank manifold.
methods.results_note: Paper reports faster convergence and more robustness to learning rate with SGD and AdamW on GPT-2, Mistral-7B and diffusion models, with negligible overhead.

relations.note: A scalar A/B learning-rate ratio is a crude special case of per-factor preconditioning.
LoRA-FA's B-gradient correction is one half of this preconditioner.

methods.name: QLoRA
methods.paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(target_modules='all-linear') on a bitsandbytes 4-bit NF4 model + prepare_model_for_kbit_training
methods.formula_latex: h=\mathrm{dequant}\big(W_0^{NF4}\big)\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\ \ W_0^{NF4} \text{ frozen 4-bit NormalFloat (double-quantized constants)},\ A,B \text{ in bf16}
methods.locus: all linear layers of a 4-bit quantized model
methods.structure: LoRA on a frozen 4-bit NF4 backbone with double quantization and paged optimizers
methods.mergeable_reason: Merging requires dequantizing the backbone (or re-quantizing after merge).
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 relative to the quantized model.
methods.key_idea: Backpropagate through a frozen 4-bit model into LoRA adapters, making 65B fine-tuning fit on one 48GB GPU.
methods.results_note: Paper reports fine-tuning a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU and Guanaco reaching 99.3% of ChatGPT's level on the Vicuna benchmark.

relations.note: LoRA applied to all linear layers of a quantized base.
LoftQ initializes LoRA to compensate quantization error.
QA-LoRA keeps the merged model quantized.

methods.name: LoRA layer replication (DUS)
methods.full_name: Memory-efficient depth up-scaling with per-replica LoRA
methods.paper_title: SOLAR 10.7B: Scaling Large Language Models with Simple yet Effective Depth Up-Scaling
methods.formula_latex: f=\ell_{\pi(L')}\circ\cdots\circ\ell_{\pi(1)},\ \ \pi:[L']\to[L] \text{ (stacked layer ranges, base weights shared)};\ W^{(j)}=W_{0,\pi(j)}+B^{(j)}A^{(j)} \text{ (distinct LoRA per replica)}
methods.locus: whole transformer stack (layer duplication) plus LoRA on every replica
methods.structure: depth up-scaling by repeating layer ranges (mergekit passthrough convention) with weight sharing, differentiated by per-replica low-rank updates
methods.mergeable_reason: Merging requires materializing separate weights for each replica, yielding a larger (deeper) model rather than the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity of the original model: replication changes depth; each replica's LoRA starts at B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Grow a model's depth by reusing its own layers, then specialize the copies cheaply with LoRA instead of storing duplicated weights.

relations.note: LoRA adapters attached to replicated layers.

methods.name: KappaTune
methods.paper_title: The Condition Number as a Scale-Invariant Proxy for Information Encoding in Neural Units
methods.formula_latex: \kappa(W)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(W)}{\sigma_{\min}(W)};\ \ \mathcal{S}=\text{lowest-}\kappa \text{ top-}p \text{ fraction of tensors};\ \text{train (or attach LoRA to) } W\in\mathcal{S},\ \text{freeze the rest}
methods.locus: module selection over all linear layers and fused MoE expert parameters
methods.structure: data-free target selection by spectral condition number (most isotropic tensors are adapted)
methods.mergeable_reason: Selected parameters or LoRAs are ordinary weight changes.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits from the chosen tuner (LoRA: B = 0).
methods.key_idea: Well-conditioned (low-kappa, high-entropy) tensors encode less specialized information and can absorb new tasks with less forgetting.
methods.results_note: Paper reports about 6x lower forgetting than LoRA on OLMoE and 2.8x lower with KappaTune-LoRA on DeepSeek-V2-Lite.

relations.note: KappaTune-LoRA places LoRA only on low-kappa modules.

methods.name: TIES-Merging
methods.paper_title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
methods.formula_latex: \hat\tau_t=\mathrm{trim}_k(\tau_t);\ \gamma=\mathrm{sgn}\Big(\sum_t\hat\tau_t\Big);\ \tau_m^{(p)}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}^p|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{A}^p}\hat\tau_t^{(p)},\ \mathcal{A}^p=\{t:\mathrm{sgn}(\hat\tau_t^{(p)})=\gamma^{(p)}\};\ W=W_0+\lambda\tau_m
methods.locus: LoRA adapters (A/B separately, or full Delta W followed by SVD for *_svd)
methods.structure: coordinate-wise trimming, sign election and disjoint averaging of task vectors
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged adapter is a single LoRA that can itself be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (post-hoc).
methods.key_idea: Merging fails mainly through redundant small values and sign conflicts; trim them and average only agreeing coordinates.
methods.results_note: Paper reports TIES outperforming existing merging methods across modalities, model sizes, architectures and fine-tuning settings.

relations.note: Refines plain task-vector addition.
DARE drop-and-rescale is used as a pre-step (dare_ties).

methods.name: DARE
methods.paper_title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
methods.formula_latex: \tilde\delta=\frac{m\odot\delta}{1-p},\ \ m\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1-p)^{\otimes\dim\delta};\ \text{then linear or TIES merge of the } \tilde\delta_t
methods.structure: random sparsification of delta parameters with unbiased rescaling before merging
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged adapter is a single LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (post-hoc).
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning deltas are extremely redundant; randomly dropping most of them and rescaling preserves ability and reduces merge interference.
methods.results_note: Paper reports dropping 90% (even 99%) of delta parameters without performance loss and gains from merging homologous models (e.g. WizardLM + WizardMath).

Sparsified task vectors.

papers.title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Fine-tuning large pretrained LMs can be done in a random low-dimensional subspace (a few hundred dimensions reach 90% of full performance on MRPC with RoBERTa), and pretraining lowers this intrinsic dimension.
papers.relevance: Foundational justification for every low-dimensional PEFT parameterization (LoRA, VeRA, Uni-LoRA, TinyLoRA are explicit subspace choices).

papers.title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
papers.claim: Adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA can all be written as modifications to specific hidden states, differing in function form, insertion position (sequential/parallel) and composition (additive/gated/scaled).
papers.relevance: First explicit unifying framework of PEFT methods; a direct precursor of a categorical classification by locus and composition law.

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.claim: For fully connected networks, LoRA can exactly adapt any model to a smaller target model once the rank exceeds a threshold depending on width and depth ratio, with quantified approximation error below it.
papers.relevance: Gives a theoretical expressivity yardstick for comparing rank-bounded (LoRA) against high-rank structured updates (HiRA, C3A, RandLoRA).

papers.title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
papers.claim: LoRA-trained weights contain new high-ranking singular vectors ('intruder dimensions') absent in full fine-tuning; they cause forgetting, and scaling them down recovers pretraining behaviour with little task loss.
papers.relevance: Spectral invariant distinguishing additive low-rank updates from full fine-tuning; implemented in HF PEFT as peft.tuners.lora.intruders.reduce_intruder_dimension (v0.19).

papers.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
papers.claim: Task vectors (fine-tuned minus pretrained weights) can be added, negated and combined arithmetically to steer model behaviour.
papers.relevance: Defines the vector-space (module) structure on adapters that PEFT's add_weighted_adapter (linear/svd/cat), TIES, DARE and GenKnowSub operate in.

papers.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
papers.claim: On code and math continued pretraining and instruction tuning, LoRA underperforms full fine-tuning but better preserves source-domain performance; full fine-tuning learns perturbations of 10-100x higher rank.
papers.relevance: Quantifies the learning/forgetting trade-off induced by restricting the update to a low-rank subobject.

papers.title: The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics
papers.claim: Initializing B = 0 with random A (the default) allows larger stable learning rates and better feature learning than the symmetric choice A = 0 with random B.
papers.relevance: Explains why identity-at-init via a zero factor is not symmetric, informing the 'identity_at_init' axis of the taxonomy.

papers.title: LoRA Without Regret
papers.claim: LoRA matches full fine-tuning when applied to all layers (especially MLP/MoE) and when capacity exceeds the information to learn; optimal LoRA learning rate is about 10x the full fine-tuning one; rank-1 LoRA suffices for RL.
papers.relevance: Cited in the HF PEFT LoRA docs (MoE rank budgeting); a capacity-based account of when the low-rank restriction is harmless.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Models: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.claim: Surveys PEFT algorithms (additive, selective, reparameterized, hybrid), their system costs and applications across model families.
papers.relevance: Standard additive/selective/reparameterized/hybrid taxonomy against which a categorical classification can be compared.

papers.title: Scaling Down to Scale Up: A Guide to Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Systematic overview and comparison of 40+ PEFT methods, organized as additive, selective and reparametrization-based approaches.
papers.relevance: Widely used classification of PEFT methods; a baseline taxonomy.
